fields.title: MONKFROG
fields.description:
MONKFROG is a production-ready, full-stack e-commerce application designed to sell themed merchandise. I architected this solution to simulate a real-world shopping environment, focusing on secure data handling, performance optimization, and a polished user experience. It bridges a high-performance React frontend with a scalable Django Rest Framework backend.

1.Authentication:JWT (JSON Web Tokens)
2.Services:SendGrid (Email Automation), WhiteNoise (Static Files)
3.Deployment: Vercel (Frontend), Render (Backend)

fields.title: Smart Access Hub for Urban Mobility
fields.description:
Smart Access Hub for Urban Mobility is basically the city's glow-up in app form — one smooth platform where citizens can book events, reserve public facilities, check parking in real time, and use one secure Universal QR Code for everything. Behind the scenes, admins get a powerful Command Center with live dashboards, instant stats, and a built-in AI assistant, CityBot, that answers questions using actual database insights. It cuts out the chaos of disconnected systems and makes the whole urban experience way more fluid, smart, and efficient.

💠Key Highlights

1.AI Assistant (CityBot): Powered by Google Gemini 2.0, offering voice-based, context-aware guidance using live data.
2.Live Operations Dashboard: Auto-updating every 5 seconds to track traffic, capacity, and usage trends.
3.RBAC Security: Tight JWT-based access separation for citizens and administrators.
4.Unified QR System: Encrypted passes used across events, facilities, and parking for smooth entry validation.
5.Centralized City Services: Bookings, reservations, and real-time monitoring all in one place.

fields.title: Automated CI/CD Pipeline on AWS Tech Stack
fields.description:
The project delivers a fully automated DevOps pipeline where every push to GitHub instantly rolls into a fresh Docker image and ships straight to an AWS EC2 server — no manual touching, no late-night config panic. Jenkins sits at the heart of the setup, orchestrating builds, tests, and deployments through Webhook triggers. The result? A deployment flow that’s fast, consistent, and eliminates nearly all operational overhead while keeping the Django app running like a champ.

💠Key Contributions

1.Infrastructure as Code: Set up and maintained an EC2 instance dedicated to CI/CD operations.

2.Containerization: Packaged the Django project into a Docker image for smooth, environment-independent releases.

3.Pipeline Automation: Created a Jenkinsfile that handles build → test → deploy the moment GitHub fires a Webhook.

4.System Administration: Configured Linux users, permissions, and firewall rules to ensure secure service communication.

fields.title: How I’m Building My Full-Stack & DevOps Portfolio From Scratch
fields.content:
## How I’m Building My Full-Stack & DevOps Portfolio From Scratch — And What I’m Learning Along the Way 

Every developer has that one project that becomes more than just a project.  
For me, it’s my portfolio.

I didn’t want a basic “Hi, I’m X” website with two buttons and a list of skills.  
I wanted something that actually *represents* who I am:

- A full-stack developer who builds things  
- A DevOps enthusiast who deploys things  
- A problem solver who loves systems, automation, and clean engineering

So I started building my portfolio from scratch — **as a real, end-to-end full-stack + DevOps product.**  
And honestly… it’s been one of the most exciting builds of my life.

---

## The Goal: A Portfolio That Doesn’t Just Show My Skills — It *Runs* Them

I didn’t want a static website.  
I wanted a **living system**.

Something that:

- tracks who visits  
- shows real-time analytics  
- has an admin dashboard  
- stores files like a mini cloud drive  
- includes a blogging system  
- uses modern animations and 3D elements  
- looks clean on every screen  
- and feels like a product, not a resume

---

##The Tech I Chose (And Why)

### **Frontend — React + Tailwind + Framer Motion**
Because I wanted:

- smooth animations  
- clean components  
- responsiveness  
- full control over UI  

React gives me that superpower.

---

### **Backend — Django + DRF + PostgreSQL**
I needed something:

- stable  
- secure  
- scalable  
- perfect for analytics + dashboard + blogging  

Django is a beast for this.

---

### **DevOps — Docker, Nginx, CI/CD**
This is the part I enjoy the most.

I wanted my portfolio to actually show my DevOps side:

- containerized services  
- automatic deployment  
- reverse proxy  
- proper HTTPS  
- logs + uptime monitoring  

Basically… a mini production-grade deployment.

---

## The Coolest Part: The Visitor Analytics System

Most portfolios don’t even know if someone opens the page.

Mine?

- Tracks every unique visitor  
- Logs every page they visit  
- Shows real-time active users  
- Displays geo-location  
- Has a full dashboard where *I* can view everything  

It’s my own tiny version of Google Analytics — built by me.

---

## The Admin Dashboard I Always Wanted

Inside my hidden admin panel, I can:

- manage projects  
- manage certifications  
- upload and download files  
- write and publish blogs  
- check analytics  
- control content  
- view system health  

It feels like logging into my own startup.

---

## The Feature That Makes Everyone Go “WOW”

### **AI-powered personal assistant.**  
A chatbot trained on **my portfolio**, **my projects**, and **my skills**.

Visitors can ask:

- “What has he built?”  
- “Explain his EMS project.”  
- “What DevOps tools does he know?”  
- “Show me his certifications.”  

And the bot answers — like an interactive resume.

This one feature alone took the portfolio from “cool” → **“bro what is this masterpiece??”**

---

## What I’ve Learned Building This

### 🔸 Full-stack is fun  
But *full-stack + DevOps* is a different level of satisfaction.

### 🔸 Deployment is not the end — monitoring is  
Seeing your own dashboard update with live visitors is magical.

### 🔸 UI matters  
Even a simple animation can make the whole site feel premium.

### 🔸 Building something for yourself hits different  
This portfolio taught me more than many courses combined.

---

## What’s Next?

I’m not done.  
I’m still adding:

- better 3D elements  
- more blogs  
- performance optimizations  
- new admin tools  
- and maybe a “guest mode” for friends to test features  

This portfolio will grow with me.

It’s not just a website.  
It’s my **developer identity** — engineered from scratch.

---

## Final Thought

If you’re a developer, build your portfolio like it’s your *biggest project*.  
Not something you make in one day…  
but something that evolves with your journey.

It will teach you:

- design  
- backend  
- deployments  
- debugging  
- UX  
- and storytelling
